 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.387/2024  :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Ranganatha S/o Rangashetty in a Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 06.07.2023 at about 00.10 a.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Ranganatha was driving an Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-7625 from Shankara Matt to Geleyarabalaga bus stop and when he reached near Dr. Rajkumar Play ground, Geleyarabalaga main road, Bengaluru, at that time, one vehicle came from opposite direction and to avoid an accident with the vehicle, said Ranganatha turned his vehicle to right side of the road.

On the right side of the road, one Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875 was parked negligently in no parking zone without any parking signal / indicator and Ranganatha's auto dashed against the Maruthi SCCH 15 4 MVC No.387/2024 Van.
Due to the impact, Ranganatha had sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

Thereafter,
Postmortem was conducted at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru and then body was handed over to the Petitioners.
Petitioners had spent about Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.

Mamatha D vs Nagaraja C on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47784350/
2 3.
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as an auto driver and was earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Ranganatha, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondents appeared before the Court through their SCCH 15 5 MVC No.387/2024 respective Counsels and the Respondent No.2 filed its Objection Statement to the main petition.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the negligent parking of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Ranganatha in the said accident.

Further it contended that as per FIR,
Charge sheet and Sketch the entire negligence on the part of the deceased / driver of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01--AH-7625 who has driven the vehicle at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875 from behind, as Omni car was parking on the extreme right side of the said road.
Further it contended that the deceased had no DL to drive the auto at the time of accident.
There is no actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Omni car.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the SCCH 15 6 MVC No.387/2024 Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

5. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Ranganatha S/o Rangashetty was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 06.07.2023 at about 0.10 a.m., opposite to Dr. Rajkumar Play Ground, Geleyarabalaga main road,
Bengaluru, due to the negligent parking of the driver of the Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Ranganatha S/o Rangashetty?

3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?

The learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied on the following decision:

, my answer to the above Issues are as under:

 REASONS 8. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the Ranganatha was died in the accident that occurred due to negligent parking of the offending Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875 by its driver.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the negligent parking of the offending van by its driver.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P13.

Ex.P-1 & 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which was lodged by one Manoj G S/o SCCH 15 9 MVC No.387/2024 Govindaraj Shetty and the Rajajinagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the deceased i.e., driver of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-7625 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 & 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to multiploe injuries sustained.
However blood and viscera are sent for chemical analysis.

Ex.P-6 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the Mamatha D vs Nagaraja C on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47784350/
4 vehicles.

Ex.P-7 is the true copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the Rajajinagar Traffic Police has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Maruthi Van for the offences punishable under Section 283 of IPC.

Further, the deceased Ranganatha was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
12.

To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer by name P. Ramesh as SCCH 15 10 MVC No.387/2024 RW.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.R.1 and 2.
13.
PW.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
In the cross- examination he deposed that he did not witness the accident and he does not know against whom Charge sheet filed after investigation.
Further he admitted that the Omni Car driver has parked his vehicle on the right side of the road and accident was not occurred by the fault of the car driver.
In the cross- examination RW.1 has deposed that they issued Notice to the owner of the offending vehicle and they did not get the Acknowledgment for the service of said Notice to the owner.
Further he deposed that he does not know the Respondent No.1 has parked his vehicle in the place where no parking board was installed.
Upon going through the police records shows that the auto came to the right side and dashed against the parked Omni car.

The Charge-sheet also shows that after the entire investigation, the IO has filed Charge sheet against the deceased Ranganath for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and SCCH 15 11 MVC No.387/2024 304(A) of IPC and Charge sheet also filed against the driver of the Omni car for his negligent parking on the road.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the deceased Ranganath and driver of the Maruthi Van for the alleged accident and in the said accident,
Ranganath was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "partly in the Affirmative".
14. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
15.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 is the son and Petitioner No.3 is the father of the deceased Ranganatha.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced her Aadhaar card and Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.2 and 3 and the deceased and Ration card at Ex.P.8, 9, 12 & 13 & 10.
The said documents shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
As the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.387/2024 Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Ranganatha, they entitled for the compensation.
16. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 46 years and deceased was working as an auto driver and was earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.

Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/-
per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.

Mamatha D vs Nagaraja C on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47784350/
5 17.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Ranganatha as 46 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.12 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Ranganatha which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1977.
The alleged accident was occurred on 06.07.2023.

That means,
as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Ranganatha was 46 years, 6 months and 05 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Ranganatha to be taken at 47 years for the purpose of assessment.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
19.
The deceased has left behind him his wife, son and father.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife,
Petitioner No.2 is the son and the Petitioner No.3 is the father and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that:
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.387/2024 rate of 10%
in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.

Further,
the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

20. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife, son and father of the deceased Ranganatha, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
21.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 is the minor son and he lost his father's love and care and the Petitioner No.3 is the father and he lost her son's love and care.

Bearing in mind the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.387/2024 relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:

6 22.
The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
23.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.16,000/- pm.
24.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
 SCCH 15 16 MVC No.387/2024 Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn.
Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
 "Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged : 21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "
- Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40

7 observed that: In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 25% when the age is between 40 to 50 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 47 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs.16,000/- comes to Rs.4,000/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + SCCH 15 18 MVC No.387/2024 Rs.4,000/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 13.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to held that where the number of dependents of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3 rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

25. After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.20,000/-, it comes to Rs.13,333/-
(Rs.20,000/- - 6,667/-) and multiplier applied is 13 which comes to Rs.20,79,948/- (13,333 x 12 x 13).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,79,948/- towards loss of dependency.

26. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,45,200/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.387/2024  3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
 4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/-
 5. Expenses of transportation of Rs. 5,000/-
 dead body  6. Loss of Dependency Rs.20,79,948/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.23,16,448/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

27. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the deceased Ranganath and negligent parking of the driver of the Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MB-9875.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.

Therefore, the SCCH 15 20 MVC Mamatha D vs Nagaraja C on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47784350/
8 No.387/2024 Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy 50% of the award amount out of the total award amount.

sentences.text: The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.3 is "Partly in the Affirmative."
28. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,16,448/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,16,448/-
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.387/2024 along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and severally are liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount, out of the total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners.

However, Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the 50%
compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 60% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 25% to the Petitioner No. 2.
3) 15% to the Petitioner No.3.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent SCCH 15 22 MVC No.387/2024 No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 , 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, till he attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.2 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.

The Charge-sheet also shows that after the entire investigation, the IO has filed Charge sheet against the deceased Ranganath for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and SCCH 15 11 MVC No.387/2024 304(A) of IPC and Charge sheet also filed against the driver of the Omni car for his negligent parking on the road.

Ranganath was succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/-
per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
The alleged accident was occurred on 06.07.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased Ranganatha to be taken at 47 years for the purpose of assessment.
Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on SCCH 15 17 MVC No.387/2024 account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork: executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,16,448/-
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.387/2024 along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and severally are liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount, out of the total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners.
However, Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the 50%
compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.
Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 60% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 25% to the Petitioner No. 2.

The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, till he attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.2 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.
